The first video related to camera tracking I've seen is here: https://www.blenderguru.com/tutorials/introduction-to-camera-tracking

As you can see, it's quite old, but the process hasn't changed much, and you'll find newer videos without my help. Basically you take some footage, define tracking points, and let the software track those points on the footage. When you have enough tracked points, it's possible to determine their position in 3d space, and create a cloud of those points, and match the cameras position and movement according to those points. That sounds very technical, but it's easier, when you see it.

If you get a good enough tracking solution, you can position points in your model according to those points. With those points, you could easily position walls, determine, how high those walls are, where some door or object is, general distances, and so on. This would give you a good starting point, after which you can position everything optically by using the cameras position as an overlay/guide.

You probably won't get a good tracking solution from st. tarrants video, but it will suffice as a starting point, which requires some manual tweaking. And you should first practice with something easier, because tracking st. tarrants video will be frustrating, even if you know, what you're doing.
